sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

paragraphs.en: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out.
paragraphs.zh: 在一项开创性研究表明莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展后，这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福文法学校的男孩，在学术争论中有力地回击了一拳。不过，前提是你得把他的作品演出来。

paragraphs.en: A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. “The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
paragraphs.zh: 一项研究发现，用“排练室”的方式教授莎士比亚作品，既扩大了儿童的词汇量，提高了他们写作的复杂程度，也提升了他们理解和表达情感的能力。委托开展这项研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）的雅基·奥汉隆说：“研究表明，演员的工作方式，会大大影响儿童使用语言的方式，以及他们看待自己的方式。”

paragraphs.en: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils—aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.” They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest. The target group were given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
paragraphs.zh: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名五年级学生，年龄为九到十岁；这些学校此前没有接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学法。学生被分为实验组和对照组，并被要求写作，例如以《暴风雨》中遭遇海难后的斐迪南的身份，写一封漂流瓶中的信。实验组在阅读选段时，还参加了一项30分钟的戏剧活动。

paragraphs.en: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length. They also “appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character’s emotion”. The Time to Act study, which is published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
paragraphs.zh: 经过同行评审的结果表明，实验组学生使用的词汇范围更广，会使用被归为更复杂或更罕见的词，文章也写得更长。他们似乎还更能自如地以角色身份写作：对照组学生想象的是自己遭遇海难时会有什么反应，而实验组学生则站在文学人物的立场上，表达那个人物的情感。皇家莎士比亚剧团本周发表的《行动起来》研究还发现，对照组学生依赖棕榈树等“荒岛描写的陈词滥调”，实验组学生的描写则更丰富，对天空、海洋和天气状况呈现出更广阔的图景。

paragraphs.en: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”. She added “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.” The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
paragraphs.zh: 奥汉隆说，最让她惊讶的是实验组儿童写作中明显体现出的情感理解和表达能力，以及他们在写作中表现得更坚韧、更充满希望。她补充说：“他们对情感的理解非常明显，这可能与排练室的过程有关，在这个过程中，你习惯于努力通过想象去体会。他们能自如地描绘不同的情绪状态，而戏剧活动的一部分就是设身处地地体会不同人物。”她说，这项研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

paragraphs.en: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，随便换一位剧作家，能否重复得到这样的结果呢？奥汉隆说，还需要更多研究，但她指出，莎士比亚使用两万个词，而日常语言使用约两千个词，这使儿童生活中的语言获得了极大拓展；与此同时，儿童还会调动全身，让这些文字鲜活起来。

notes.text: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils—aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.”
notes.translation: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名九到十岁五年级学生，这些学校此前没有接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学法。
notes.hint: 主干为 The trial involved pupils；aged nine and ten 是插入的年龄说明；that had not been...修饰 schools，说明学校此前未接触该教学法。

notes.text: They also “appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character’s emotion”.
notes.translation: 他们似乎也更能自如地以角色身份写作：对照组学生想象的是自己遭遇海难时的反应，实验组学生则站在文学人物的立场上表达该人物的情感。
notes.hint: appear to be 后接 comfortable；writing in role 指以角色身份写作。while 引出对照，how...是 imagine 的宾语从句；put oneself in someone’s shoes 表示设身处地。

notes.text: The Time to Act study, which is published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
notes.translation: 皇家莎士比亚剧团本周发表的《行动起来》研究还发现，对照组学生依赖棕榈树等荒岛描写的陈词滥调，而实验组学生对天空、海洋和天气状况的描写更丰富、更开阔。
notes.hint: 主干为 The study found that...；which...补充研究的发表情况。that 内部的 while 对比两组表现；such as palm trees 举例说明 clichés。

notes.text: O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
notes.translation: 奥汉隆说还需要更多研究，但指出莎士比亚使用两万个词，相比之下日常语言使用约两千个词，这极大地拓展了儿童生活中的语言，并与儿童调动全身使文字鲜活起来相结合。

sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

paragraphs.en: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
paragraphs.zh: 我最近得知，一些科学家想要缩减研究规模，以减少碳排放，这让我十分震惊。他们说，危机已经到来，我们需要减少耗能密集的建模工作。至少，我们需要让能源使用变得可持续得多。

paragraphs.en: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 percent of the world’s electricity.
paragraphs.zh: 无可争辩，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星，也就是我们科学家用来测量地球脉搏的工具，无论在建造时还是运行中，都需要大量能源。同样，科学对信息永不满足的需求，导致世界各地耗能密集的数据中心迅速增多，这也是事实。根据国际能源署的数据，这些设施目前消耗了全球约1%的电力。

paragraphs.en: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这是我们为了理解世界而必须付出的代价。如果我们无法追踪大气中的二氧化碳含量、它来自哪里，以及是谁排放的，又怎么能告诉决策者，减少碳排放的最佳方式是什么呢？技术研究所产生的碳排放是值得的：这些研究最终将守护地球的未来。

paragraphs.en: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate change and to do nothing. But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action: she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting emissions.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家要向公众说明这一道理，可能很困难，因为我们的工作很复杂，常在不对外开放的场所开展，也并不总是容易阐释或解释。但是，如果我们要解决人类最重大的难题，就必须展示科学的实际成效。面对气候变化等令人畏惧的问题，人很容易感到束手无策，什么都不做。但这时，我会想起一位朋友的女儿，她把恐惧转化为行动：她成为了一名风能工程师，如今在提供可再生能源、限制排放的工作中干劲十足。

paragraphs.en: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world’s solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.
paragraphs.zh: 认识到科学和工程能够带来希望，是设立千禧年技术奖的动力；这个表彰人类创造才智的奖项如今已进入第20个年头。历届获奖者之一、澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授，是钝化发射极和背面电池技术的发明者，这项技术如今被用于世界上大多数太阳能电池板。得益于他的发明，我们才真正有机会减少全球碳排放。

paragraphs.en: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
paragraphs.zh: 每一天，科学家、技术人员和工程师都在发现利用可再生能源的新方法，开发新技术，不仅让能源使用更智能，也为我们的智能活动提供能源。一个很好的例子是位于芬兰的欧洲最大超级计算机LUMI，它竟然实现了负碳排放。它建在一座旧造纸厂里，由附近河流提供能源，其产生的热量为周边卡亚尼镇居民供暖。

paragraphs.en: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
paragraphs.zh: 如果世界要实现净零排放的目标，我们就必须认真思考，如何实现可持续计算，并建成更多像LUMI这样的系统。

sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

paragraphs.en: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
paragraphs.zh: 自从在奈飞擅长的领域与其展开竞争以来，传统好莱坞一直难以从流媒体业务中获利，迪士尼+、孔雀和派拉蒙+等平台每年亏损数十亿美元，这令人担忧这些服务永远无法像过去的有线电视那样赚钱。但流媒体时代却让一些意料之外的赢家受益：盗版者利用软件，几秒钟就能从合法在线视频平台复制一部电影或电视节目，再把这些作品放到他们自己的非法平台上。这些平台每年从广告和订阅中攫取约20亿美元。

paragraphs.en: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that's working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.
paragraphs.zh: 据美国电影协会（MPA）称，由于无需承担视频制作成本，非法流媒体网站的利润率已接近90%。该协会是代表好莱坞制片公司的行业组织，正致力于打击近年来大量涌现的非法平台。

paragraphs.en: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center. The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，奈飞等合法网络企业的兴起实际上有助于遏制数字盗版，当时的盗版主要依靠上传文件。但美国商会全球创新政策中心估计，如今涉及非法流媒体服务及文件共享的盗版活动，每年给美国经济造成约300亿美元的收入损失，并使约25万个工作岗位流失。它对全球造成的经济影响每年约为710亿美元。

paragraphs.en: "The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations," says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. "This is organized crime." Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
paragraphs.zh: 美国电影协会首席执行官查理·里夫金说：“那些窃取我们的电影和电视节目、经营盗版网站的人，并非夫妻店式的小本经营者。这是有组织犯罪。”里夫金于2017年加入该协会；五年前，协会曾试图促成好莱坞与硅谷达成共识，以推动国会通过旨在阻止网络盗版的立法，但没有成功。2017年，协会成立了创意与娱乐联盟（ACE），这是一个由大约100名调查员组成的执法工作组。他们在全球各地活动，协助地方当局逮捕流媒体盗版者。

paragraphs.en: ACE says it's helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA's support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyright material a serious crime.
paragraphs.zh: 创意与娱乐联盟表示，它已帮助把北美非法流媒体服务的数量从2018年的1400多个减少到126个。这在一定程度上得益于美国电影协会对2020年一项联邦法律的支持，该法律将大规模播放受版权保护材料的流媒体盗版行为定为重罪。

paragraphs.en: Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. "While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline," says analyst Steve Hawley.
paragraphs.zh: 咨询公司Parks Associates预测，自2022年以来，美国合法流媒体服务因盗版遭受的累计损失将在未来两年达到1130亿美元。分析师史蒂夫·霍利说：“虽然有人乐观地认为，新出现的应对措施和最佳做法可能使盗版到2027年开始进入平台期，但对于盗版何时才会开始减少，各利益相关方尚未达成共识。”

sections.title: 阅读理解 · Text 4
sections.subtitle: 36–40题 · 10分
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

paragraphs.en: Visit any antiques store and you'll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-1965 World's Fair, the ephemera of history. Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible.
paragraphs.zh: 走进任何一家古董店，你都会遇到过去留下的物品：照片、信件、一本详细介绍1964—1965年世界博览会辛克莱恐龙展览的小册子——这些都是历史中原本短暂存在的物件。然而，这些东西并非真的转瞬即逝，因为几十年、甚至几百年以后，它们仍然存在。为什么？因为它们是有形的。

paragraphs.en: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on. Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
paragraphs.zh: 考虑到这些资料的制作者很少为长期保存做好安排，你是否思考过无形形式、也就是数字信息的生命周期？几千年来，我们之所以能够了解已有的知识，靠的是留存下来的物品，即使最初的制作者往往并未加以照管。物品本身就是传递信息的媒介。这些材料在制作之初并未得到有意的保存，但非数字化材料仍有机会留存下来，成为传记作家、历史学家和小说家所依赖的历史记录。图书馆和档案馆历来承担着整理、保存信息以及提供信息获取渠道的责任。因此，图书馆员把有形资料数字化，使全世界的研究者都能快速检索和获取馆藏。结果是历史资料丰富得令人应接不暇，而这本身也带来了如同大海捞针般的检索难题。

paragraphs.en: Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cellphone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
paragraphs.zh: 当用户举着手机说“全都在这里面”，以人人都能获取信息为证据，说明如今图书馆对研究者已不那么重要时，图书馆员的无私奉献反而可能对我们不利。然而，这种普遍的信息获取是如何成为可能的？也许更重要的是，它又如何得到维持？谁来管理保存下来的资料？说到原生数字信息，一个可怕的答案可能是：如果图书馆员和档案工作者不做，就没人来做。数字信息比非数字化信息需要多得多的照料。

paragraphs.en: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replace analog.
paragraphs.zh: 即使一份数字资料被保存下来，留下的也可能仅仅是载体，而非信息本身。随着技术进步、某种格式过时，这份资料就会失去用途。你是否曾无助地盯着一张ZIP磁盘，心想：怎样才能从这里面取出文件？如果不持续迁移数字资源，历史学家就会因一个可预见的未来噩梦而夜不能寐：当数字形式取代非数字形式时，历史记录却突然中断了。

paragraphs.en: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名日常工作围绕特藏和数字资源展开的图书馆员，我也体会到历史学家夜间的恐惧；如果说现在已经有了全面的保存方案，那就是在撒谎。不过，研究者仍可从这样一个事实中得到些许安慰：众多图书馆员正在致力于发现、整理和保存数字信息，为当下和未来的研究者服务。图书馆员处在独特的位置，能够了解最终用户如何寻找和使用信息。因此，我们在识别、保存数字资料并提供获取途径方面发挥着不可或缺的作用，使未来的研究者即使觉得在数字领域开展研究很有挑战，也不至于认为那是不可能的。

notes.translation: 考虑到这些资料的制作者很少为长期保存做好安排，你是否思考过无形形式、也就是数字信息的生命周期？
notes.hint: 主句是 Have you pondered the life cycle…；digital information解释intangible formats。given that意为“考虑到”，引导条件背景；who从句修饰those。make provision for是“为……做好安排”。

notes.hint: 主干是 Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us。when从句说明情形；by…表示用户举证的方式；that从句解释evidence的内容，即用户据此得出的判断，并非作者认同的结论。

sections.subtitle: 41–45题 · 10分
sections.directions: The following paragraphs are given in a wrong order. For questions 41–45, you are required to reorganize these paragraphs into a coherent text by choosing from the list A–H and filling them into the numbered boxes. Paragraphs A, C, and H have been correctly placed. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

paragraphs.en: A. Peters likes to photograph butterflies in a landscape, celebrating the beauty of their surroundings as well as the insects themselves. His pictures of a Glanville fritillary rising from the sea-pinks beside the chalk cliffs of Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight are particularly glorious. These take-off shots are even more challenging because they require a wide-angle lens, which means he must be less than 2cm from the butterfly. It's incredibly difficult to get that close to a skittish sun-warmed insect. Unlike some photographers, who “cheat” by keeping insects in a fridge to slow them down, Peters refuses to tamper with wild butterflies.
paragraphs.zh: A. 彼得斯喜欢把蝴蝶放在风景中拍摄，既展现昆虫本身，也赞美周围环境的美。他拍到一只格兰维尔豹蛱蝶从怀特岛康普顿湾白垩悬崖边的海石竹花丛中腾起，画面尤其绚丽。这类起飞照片更具挑战，因为要用广角镜头，这意味着他必须离蝴蝶不到2厘米。如此接近一只被太阳晒暖、容易受惊的昆虫，难度极大。有些摄影师通过把昆虫放进冰箱来减缓它们的活动，借此“作弊”，而彼得斯拒绝人为摆弄野生蝴蝶。

paragraphs.en: B. Peters' signature shot is a butterfly “take-off”, showing the multiple wing-beats of one butterfly in one frame as it lifts off from a flower. How does he capture it? Technology helps. A typical digital SLR camera shoots 20 frames a second. He uses a high-speed OM System which shoots 120 frames a second.
paragraphs.zh: B. 彼得斯的标志性照片是蝴蝶“起飞”：在一个画面中呈现同一只蝴蝶从花上飞起时多次拍动翅膀的情形。他如何捕捉？技术帮了忙。典型数码单反相机每秒拍摄20帧，他使用的高速OM System相机则每秒拍摄120帧。

paragraphs.en: C. Britain has relatively few butterfly species compared with mainland Europe and 80% are in decline, mostly because intensive chemical farming has reduced many species to tiny fragments of habitat and small nature reserves. Global heating is benefiting some species but others are too isolated to find suitable new habitat, and gardening habits—paving over gardens and using pesticides—aren't helping either. Butterflies may not pollinate as many plants as wild bees and hoverflies, but because British butterflies are the best-studied group of insects in the world, they are an extremely useful indicator of the wider declines in flying insects.
paragraphs.zh: C. 与欧洲大陆相比，英国的蝴蝶种类相对较少，其中80%的种类数量正在下降，主要因为大量使用化学品的集约农业使许多物种的栖息地缩减为零碎的小片区域和小型自然保护区。全球变暖有利于某些物种，但另一些物种过于孤立，无法找到合适的新栖息地；将花园铺成硬地和使用杀虫剂等园艺习惯也无益于它们。蝴蝶授粉的植物种类或许不如野蜂和食蚜蝇多，但英国蝴蝶是世界上研究最充分的昆虫群体，因此可以作为衡量飞行昆虫整体衰退状况的极有用指标。

paragraphs.en: D. Five years ago, at summer's end, Andrew Fusek Peters was diagnosed with bowel cancer. “I was waiting for surgery, feeling really ill, sitting in my garden. It was amazing weather and there were painted lady butterflies everywhere,” he says. “They were a symbol of fragile life, of hope and defiance, and something appealed to my soul.”
paragraphs.zh: D. 五年前夏末，安德鲁·富塞克·彼得斯被诊断出肠癌。他说：“我当时坐在花园里等手术，身体很不舒服。天气好极了，到处都是红蛱蝶。它们象征着脆弱的生命、希望与不屈，有什么东西触动了我的灵魂。”

paragraphs.en: E. That makes it sound easy, and artificial, but Peters insists it is still a massive challenge. He typically takes between 10,000 and 20,000 shots to get one butterfly take-off sequence in focus. At such high shutter speeds, the depth of field is tiny, and as butterflies do not fly in a straight line they swiftly flutter out of focus. As well as thousands of attempts, it takes patience and fieldcraft to anticipate a butterfly's likely flight-line—and catch it—in focus.
paragraphs.zh: E. 这听起来似乎容易，而且颇为人为，但彼得斯坚称挑战依然很大。他通常要拍一万至两万张照片，才能得到一组对焦清晰的蝴蝶起飞画面。在如此高的快门速度下，景深极小；蝴蝶又不沿直线飞行，因此很快就飞出焦点范围。除了成千上万次尝试，还需要耐心与野外技巧，才能预判蝴蝶可能的飞行路线，并清晰地捕捉它。

paragraphs.en: F. So what's the appeal of a long, sweaty day in pursuit of an elusive, fast-moving wild animal? “It just feels bloody brilliant,” says Peters. “If I've had a full day of good encounters with butterflies, met interesting butterfly people and I've got some good shots, that becomes a vault in my spiritual bank. It's a happy feeling.”
paragraphs.zh: F. 那么，为追逐难以捕捉、行动迅速的野生动物，辛苦流汗一整天，吸引力何在？彼得斯说：“那感觉简直太棒了。如果一整天都和蝴蝶美好相遇，遇到了有趣的蝴蝶爱好者，又拍到了几张好照片，这就成了我精神银行里的一座宝库。那是一种幸福的感觉。”

paragraphs.en: G. A children's author and poet who had become a keen amateur photographer, Peters watched the butterflies and idly wondered if he could capture them in flight. It swiftly became an obsession as he recovered from a successful operation to remove the cancer. In recent summers, he has travelled the length and breadth of Britain to photograph all 58 native species of butterfly. Now the fruits of those summers have been published in a beautiful new book.
paragraphs.zh: G. 彼得斯是一位儿童文学作家和诗人，后来成为热情的业余摄影爱好者。他看着蝴蝶，随意地想着能否拍下它们飞行的样子。成功接受癌症切除手术、逐步康复期间，这件事很快成了他的痴迷。最近几个夏天，他走遍英国，拍摄全部58种本土蝴蝶。如今，那些夏天的成果已集结成一本精美的新书。

paragraphs.en: H. A butterfly takes off so quickly it is still impossible to react quickly enough to capture that take-off but if he half-presses the shutter, the camera saves the 70 previous frames before the moment he actually takes the picture. “It's time travel, so I don't miss the moment of take-off,” he says. After he's captured the butterfly taking off, he layers 10 to 15 frames together in Photoshop.
paragraphs.zh: H. 蝴蝶起飞太快，人仍不可能及时作出反应来捕捉起飞瞬间；但如果他半按快门，相机就会保存实际按下快门之前的70帧画面。他说：“这就像时间旅行，所以我不会错过起飞的瞬间。”拍到蝴蝶起飞后，他会在Photoshop中把10至15帧叠加在一起。

sections.directions: Read the following text carefully and then translate the underlined segments into Chinese. Write your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

paragraphs.en: Innovation and research have relied on public participation in science for centuries. It was a musician who discovered the planet Uranus in the 18th century by making his own telescope with mirrors composed of copper and tin. (46) Recent decades have seen science move into a convention where engagement in the subject can only be done through institutions, such as a university. Citizen science provides an opportunity for greater public engagement and the democratisation of science.
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪以来，创新和研究一直依赖公众参与科学。18世纪，一位音乐家用铜锡合金镜面自制望远镜，发现了天王星。（46）近几十年来，科学逐渐形成了一种惯例：人们只有通过大学等机构才能参与这一领域。公众科学为更广泛的公众参与和科学民主化提供了机会。

paragraphs.en: In the information era, large data sets, small teams and financial restrictions have slowed scientific process. (47) But by utilising the natural curiosity of the general public it is possible to overcome many of these challenges by engaging non-scientists directly in the research process. Anyone can be a citizen scientist, regardless of age, nationality or academic experience. You don't even need any formal training, just an inquisitive mind and the enthusiasm to join one of the thousands of citizen science projects to generate new knowledge and the means to understand a genuine scientific outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 在信息时代，庞大的数据集、小规模团队和经费限制使科学进程放慢。（47）但利用普通公众天生的好奇心，让非科学工作者直接参与研究过程，就有可能克服其中许多挑战。无论年龄、国籍或学术经历如何，任何人都可以成为公众科学参与者。你甚至不需要正式培训，只需要好奇心和热情，加入数千个公众科学项目中的一个，创造新知识，并获得理解真实科学成果的途径。

paragraphs.en: (48) Scientists have employed a variety of ways to engage the general public in their research, such as making data analysis into an online game or sample collection into a smartphone application. They've implored citizens to help with bug counting and categorising cancer cells, and even identifying distant galaxies.
paragraphs.zh: （48）科学家采用了多种方式让普通公众参与研究，例如把数据分析变成网络游戏，或把样本采集变成智能手机应用程序。他们曾恳请公众帮助统计昆虫数量、对癌细胞分类，甚至识别遥远的星系。

paragraphs.en: This form of accessible science means that great minds are able to join the race to create and develop projects with the potential to change the world. A citizen science-based approach can extend the field of vision and include different ideas and different brains to problem-solve and create, making innovation faster and more effective.
paragraphs.zh: 这种人人可参与的科学形式，让有才智的人能够加入竞相创建和发展可能改变世界的项目的行列。基于公众科学的方法可以拓宽视野，吸收不同想法和不同头脑来解决问题、进行创造，从而使创新更快、更有效。

paragraphs.en: The rise of citizen science has grown alongside the rise of do-it-yourself biology laboratories around the world. (49) These groups of people are part of a rapidly expanding biotechnological social movement of citizen scientists and professional scientists seeking to take discovery out of institutions and put it into the hands of anyone with the enthusiasm.
paragraphs.zh: 公众科学的兴起，与世界各地自主生物学实验室的兴起同步发展。（49）这些人群是一个迅速发展的生物技术社会运动的一部分，参与者包括公众科学爱好者和专业科学家，他们力求让科学发现走出机构，交到任何有热情的人手中。

paragraphs.en: There are around 40 official do-it-yourself biology centres across the globe in locations including Paris, London, Sydney, and Tel Aviv. (50) They pool resources, collaborate, think outside the box, and find solutions and ways around obstacles to explore science for the sake of science without the traditional boundaries of working inside a formal setting. So is it time to take the Petri dish out of the laboratory and into the garage?
paragraphs.zh: 全球约有40家正式的自主生物学中心，分布在巴黎、伦敦、悉尼和特拉维夫等地。（50）他们汇集资源、开展合作、打破思维定式，寻找解决方案和克服障碍的途径，突破在正式机构内工作的传统限制，为科学本身而探索科学。那么，是不是该把培养皿从实验室搬进车库了？

questions.stem: Write an essay of 160–200 based on the following table. In your essay, you should 1) describe the table briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on the ANSWER SHEET. (20 points)
questions.stemZh: 根据表格写160–200词短文：简要描述表格，解释其含义，并发表看法。
questions.answer:
The table shows changes in the ownership of three major household appliances per 100 Chinese households between 2014 and 2023. Air conditioners recorded the most dramatic growth, rising from 75.2 to 145.9 units. Washing machines increased from 83.7 to 98.2, while refrigerators rose from 85.5 to 103.4. All three categories grew throughout the period, though at different rates.

These figures suggest a continuing improvement in living standards. As household incomes rise, families can afford appliances that make everyday life more convenient and comfortable. Meanwhile, advances in manufacturing have brought consumers a wider range of reliable products. The particularly rapid growth in air conditioner ownership may also reflect a stronger demand for comfortable indoor environments and the use of several units in one home.

In my view, this trend is encouraging because it indicates that more people can enjoy the benefits of economic development. Further progress should focus on both product quality and responsible consumption. Manufacturers should develop durable, energy-efficient appliances, while consumers should choose products suited to their needs and recycle old ones properly. In this way, better living can go hand in hand with environmental protection.

paragraphs.en: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly changing every aspect of human life. The world of AI is buzzing with an exciting potential to improve and enrich our lives. [[1]], AI also has the potential hazard of [[2]] our experiences in ways we might find difficult to control. One such [[3]] is how we understand and experience beauty.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能（AI）的进步正在迅速改变人类生活的方方面面。人工智能领域充满令人兴奋的潜力，有望改善并丰富我们的生活。不过，人工智能也可能以我们难以控制的方式主导我们的体验，带来潜在风险。其中一个这样的领域，就是我们如何理解和体验美。

paragraphs.en: AI can be a collaborative tool in a wide range of creative endeavors. [[4]] human creativity and AI algorithms can lead to unique artistic [[5]] that are beautiful to the human eye. These collaborations are likely to become increasingly common. [[6]], as convenient and provocative, AI enables virtual try-on experiences where you can virtually [[7]] makeup, hairstyles, clothing, and even cosmetic procedures [[8]] making any physical changes. Individuals can now experiment with different looks and [[9]] their preferences, potentially expanding the range of beauty ideals.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能可以成为广泛创作活动中的协作工具。将人类创造力与人工智能算法相结合，可以产生在人类眼中很美的独特艺术成果。此类合作可能会越来越普遍。例如，人工智能提供方便而能激发思考的虚拟试用体验，让你在不做任何实际改变之前，虚拟尝试化妆、发型、服装，甚至美容手术。如今，人们可以尝试不同形象，探索自己的偏好，从而可能拓宽理想美的范围。

paragraphs.en: AI algorithms can [[10]] facial features and skin conditions to provide personalized beauty recommendations. This [[11]] approach aims to cater to individual preferences and enhance the concept of beauty tailored to each person's unique characteristics. [[12]], AI can be a fun vehicle for self-discovery.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能算法可以分析面部特征和皮肤状况，从而提供个性化美容建议。这种定制方式旨在迎合个人偏好，并强化一种根据每个人独特特点量身打造的美的观念。这样一来，人工智能就可以成为一种有趣的自我探索工具。

paragraphs.en: While AI offers exciting possibilities, it also raises ethical [[13]]. There is a risk of deepening societal beauty [[14]] and perpetuating unattainable beauty standards. [[15]], AI-powered beauty filters and editing tools can lead to distorted self-perception and [[16]] body dissatisfaction. As summarized in a recent post on “The Hidden Dangers of Online Beauty Filters”, [[17]] on this technology for social presentation can cause harm [[18]] body image issues, lower self-esteem, and social anxiety.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管人工智能带来令人兴奋的可能性，它也引发伦理方面的担忧。它可能加剧社会中的容貌压力，并延续那些难以达到的审美标准。此外，人工智能美颜滤镜和编辑工具可能扭曲自我认知，并加剧人们对身体的不满。正如最近一篇《网络美颜滤镜的隐患》所总结的那样，依赖这种技术来展示自己的社交形象，可能造成身体形象问题、自尊降低和社交焦虑等伤害。

paragraphs.en: It's important to note that while AI can enhance our [[19]] of beauty, it should not [[20]] the genuine human experience and the emotional connections we derive from seeing the beauty in each other.
paragraphs.zh: 需要注意的是，虽然人工智能可以提高我们欣赏美的能力，但它不应取代真实的人类体验，以及我们从发现彼此之美中获得的情感联系。

sections.directions: Read the following text. Answer the questions after the text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.

paragraphs.en: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward. They’ve helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world. But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery. Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa—about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses. The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
paragraphs.zh: 数千年来，驴一直对推动人类文明进步至关重要。它们帮助拉车、载客，并将货物运往世界各地。但这些动物最初在何时、何地与人类产生紧密联系，一直是个谜。如今，研究人员利用两百多头驴的基因组，将驴的驯化追溯到大约七千年前东非发生的一次事件——比人类驯服马约早三千年。研究团队本月在《科学》杂志上发表了研究结果。

paragraphs.en: “Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves,” co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement. “We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened. Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived.”
paragraphs.zh: 合著者、佛罗里达大学马科动物研究人员萨曼莎·布鲁克斯在声明中说：“这些动物正通过自身的 DNA 讲述自己的历史。我们通常只能通过文字记录了解人类一方的历史，但文字记录当然并不总能准确反映事情究竟如何发生。通过研究这些 DNA 序列，我们能获得生物学证据，了解这些动物生活过的环境以及它们历经的遭遇。”

paragraphs.en: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe. They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago. The team reconstructed the animals' evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses. They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员考察了来自全球三十一个国家的现代驴的二百零七份基因组。他们还研究了十五匹野生马科动物，以及三十一头生活在大约四千年前至一百年前的古代驴的基因组。团队重建了这些动物的进化树，并利用计算机模型确定了驯化事件：肯尼亚和非洲之角的牧民驯服了野驴。随后，他们追踪这些动物如何在大约两千五百年后扩散到非洲大陆其余地区，并进入欧洲和亚洲。

paragraphs.en: Though it's still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News' Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier. “Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at going at deserts,” co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabin University in France, tells the publication. Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管最初发生驯化的原因尚不清楚，《科学新闻》的弗丽达·克赖尔报道说，这一事件恰逢撒哈拉沙漠变得更大、更干燥。合著者、法国保罗·萨宾大学进化生物学家吕多维克·奥兰多告诉该刊：“说到驮东西，驴堪称冠军，而且它们擅长在沙漠中行进。”史前人类可能为了穿越不断扩大的撒哈拉沙漠而驯服驴。

paragraphs.en: Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight. The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa. But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员说，这些发现有助于让驴受到更多关注。这些动物可以从更多研究中受益：目前，非洲赤道以南地区的驴还没有已发表的基因组。不过，了解驴最初在哪里被驯化，可以引导考古学家将搜寻范围缩小到一片区域，从而深入了解最早的家驴。

paragraphs.en: Not only does understanding the equines’ genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet's environment, write the authors.
paragraphs.zh: 作者写道，了解这些马科动物的基因构成，不仅有助于揭示它们对人类历史的贡献，而且在气候变化改变地球环境的背景下，还可能改善未来对它们的管理。

notes.hint: where and when…是整个名词性从句，作主语；谓语是 has been，表语是 a mystery。不要把 humans 当成主语。

sections.directions: Read the following text. Answer the questions after the text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.

paragraphs.en: There's no business like show business—but in Los Angeles, it feels like there's no business at all.
paragraphs.zh: 没有哪种生意能比得上演艺业——但在洛杉矶，感觉却像是根本没有生意可做。

paragraphs.en: If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that “we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession”. This is a reaction to Hollywood's decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California.
paragraphs.zh: 如果这听起来太夸张，请看看这一事实：代表约三千名影视工作者的工会——艺术指导工会——已经暂停了一项培训计划，并发表声明解释说：“我们无法昧着良心鼓励你们从事我们这一行。”这是对好莱坞衰退的回应，而这种衰退对整个行业和南加州而言，正到达一个关键节点。

paragraphs.en: Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present. Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust. Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, plus an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo.
paragraphs.zh: 影视制作自二十世纪五十年代以来就在不断从好莱坞流走，但这种影响从未像现在这样明显。美国其他地区、加拿大和欧洲持续增加激励措施，以吸引电视节目和电影制作，把加州远远甩在后面。佐治亚州对影视制作成本提供最高百分之三十的可转让税收抵免；如果作品加入佐治亚州的推广标识，还可在基础税收抵免上再增加百分之十。

paragraphs.en: Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year. We were kept afloat by “peak TV”, the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管加州有大量制作业务流向其他地方，但在今年以前，洛杉矶仍有大量影视制作活动。我们靠“电视巅峰期”维持着运转——流媒体服务爆发式增长，需要海量内容。

paragraphs.en: But 2022 was the peak of peak TV. Back then platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV hemorrhaged billions of dollars to generate content to attract new subscribers, resulting in 633 scripted series being released that year. As the streamers’ emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，二〇二二年已经是电视巅峰期的顶峰。当时，奈飞、亚马逊和 Apple TV 等平台为制作内容、吸引新订阅用户而投入数十亿美元，结果那一年推出了六百三十三部有剧本的剧集。随着流媒体平台的重点从增加订阅用户转向盈利，服务价格上升，而新剧数量下降至二〇二三年的四百八十一部；预计几年内还会降到三百多部。

paragraphs.en: If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry's essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue. Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn't offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry.
paragraphs.zh: 如果南加州的影视制作量长期低于临界水平，这个行业不可或缺的人才将会流失，巨额收入也会随之流走。如果我们无法提供充足的本地影视工作人员、演员以及支持娱乐业的本地企业，说服制片公司来这里拍摄将会困难得多。

paragraphs.en: That's why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, Film LA, now should act, before it's too late. These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles. Let's go on with the show…and make sure the show doesn't go on without us.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，加州电影委员会和与其对应的洛杉矶机构 Film LA 现在就应该行动，趁一切还来得及。这些机构与其他政府部门应该大幅改善激励措施，以留住现有节目，并吸引新的制作项目来到洛杉矶。让演出继续吧……而且要确保演出不会撇下我们继续进行。

notes.text: As the streamers’ emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years.
notes.translation: 随着流媒体平台重点从订阅用户增长转向盈利，服务价格上涨，二〇二三年新剧数量下降到四百八十一部，预计几年内还会降至三百多部。
notes.hint: As 从句说明背景及原因；主句为 prices went up 和 the number went down 两部分；with…expected to…补充对数量的预测。

sections.title: Reading · Text 3
sections.subtitle: 31–35题 · 10分
sections.directions: Read the following text. Answer the questions after the text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.

paragraphs.en: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people. Sir John Reith said that it would end “isolation of the spirit” and rejoiced: “It does not matter how many thousands may be listening, there is always enough for others. . . the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously.”
paragraphs.zh: 无线广播的先驱把它看作送给所有人的礼物。约翰·里斯爵士说，它将结束“精神上的孤立”，并欣喜地表示：“无论有成千上万的多少人在收听，总有足够的内容供其他人收听……天才与愚人、富人与穷人，都能同时收听。”

paragraphs.en: Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness. Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939. She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill.
paragraphs.zh: 在两次世界大战之间，这项技术创新塑造了一种新的国家共同意识。本周，一本书及一场由比蒂·鲁本斯策划的展览在牛津的博德利图书馆推出，记录了广播在1922年至1939年间如何改变日常生活。她采用的资料包括书信、日记、小说，以及温妮弗雷德·吉尔在1939年开展听众调查时逐字记录受访者话语的实地笔记。

paragraphs.en: There's fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness. A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they're all in headphones. People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes. A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and “talking on the brush handle”.
paragraphs.zh: 那些享受广播纯粹新鲜感的人留下的见证颇有趣味。一幅漫画嘲讽了一群无法交谈的人，因为他们全都戴着耳机。有人说，广播中的音乐让工人们吹起了新曲子。一位女士说，自从有了无线广播，街头打架少了，但人们停下脚步、“倚着扫帚柄聊天”的时候也少了。

paragraphs.en: By and large the wireless was welcome. I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered “a lot of variety. things I thought I'd never be interested in…ice hockey perhaps”. True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task. In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: “I caught up with the news, learnt some 17th-century history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope.”
paragraphs.zh: 总的来说，无线广播受到欢迎。我很喜欢20世纪30年代调查中的那位男士：他发现广播突然提供了“很多不同的东西，一些我原以为自己永远不会感兴趣的东西……也许是冰球”。的确，在数字时代到来之前的80多年里，按时间顺序播出的谈话类广播送来了不期而遇的收获，让开车途中或枯燥体力劳动中的某个时刻意外变得生动。我在自己那本关于广播的书中记下了一次开车时的经历：“我了解了最新新闻，学到了一些17世纪的历史，还意外地从一档朴实无华、介绍听诊器历史的节目中增长了见识。”

paragraphs.en: But radio's enriching serendipity is ebbing. With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when. And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，广播这种丰富生活、带来意外收获的能力正在消退。面对众多广播网络和数不清的播客，智能手机用户可以选择听什么、何时听。虽然散步时能通过耳机收听任何想听的内容很美妙，但无限的选择也会促使我们退缩到狭窄的兴趣和与自己观点相投的信念之中。

paragraphs.en: A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered? Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading. But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest. Whatever we do, innovation will happen. Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfie-vanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of “talking on the brush handle”. It's enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.
paragraphs.zh: 从马可尼和里斯所处的时代算起，一百年过去了，单纯倾听的艺术是否正面临危险？有人会说，有声书的繁荣让这种艺术复兴了，不过我想，接着你又可以担心阅读的衰落。但发明塑造着我们每一个人。当与技术有关的社会习惯确实发生变化时，值得留意，并问一问是否应稍加控制，或保护年龄最小的孩子。无论我们怎么做，创新都会发生。今天，我们为盯着手机和热衷自拍所造成的孤立文化而忧虑；然而早在1939年，就有那位女士遗憾地说，整条街的人都有了收音机以后，街上便失去了“倚着扫帚柄聊天”的邻里习惯。这足以让人放下智能手机，拿着一把院子用的扫帚走到门外去。

notes.text: Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939.
notes.translation: 本周，一本书及一场由比蒂·鲁本斯策划的展览在牛津的博德利图书馆推出，记录了广播在1922年至1939年间如何改变日常生活。
notes.hint: 主干是 a book and exhibition ... records ...；curated by ... 是过去分词短语，补充说明书与展览的策划者；how引导宾语从句，交代所记录的内容。Opening this week补充推出时间。

notes.text: And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
notes.translation: 虽然散步时能通过耳机收听任何想听的内容很美妙，但无限的选择也会促使我们退缩到狭窄的兴趣和与自己观点相投的信念之中。
notes.hint: while在这里表示“虽然”，引导让步从句；主句是 infinite choice encourages us to shrink ...。从句中的it是形式主语，真正的主语是to take a walk ...；sympathetic在此表示观点相投，不是“值得同情的”。

notes.text: But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest.
notes.translation: 但发明塑造着我们每一个人；当与技术有关的社会习惯确实发生变化时，值得留意，并问一问是否应稍加控制，或保护年龄最小的孩子。
notes.hint: and连接两个主句：inventions shape ... 与 it is worth ...。worth后的noticing和asking并列；when从句说明留意什么或何时留意，do强调“确实”；whether to ...说明所思考的问题。the youngest指年龄最小的人，语境中是孩子。

questions.stem: What can be learnt about wireless from Sir John Reith?
questions.stemZh: 从约翰·里斯爵士的话中，可以了解到无线广播的什么特点？

options.meaning: 人人都能收听它。accessible：能够接触或使用的；everyone：每个人。
它改善了人际关系。improve：改善；interpersonal relations：人际关系。

options.text: It was a miracle of human ingenuity.
options.meaning: 它是人类才智创造的奇迹。miracle：奇迹；ingenuity：聪明才智、独创性。

options.text: It led to a new era of isolating culture.
options.meaning: 它开启了孤立文化的新时代。lead to：导致、带来；era：时代；isolating：使人孤立的。

questions.explanation: 里斯说天才与愚者、富人与穷人都能同时收听，强调广播人人可用，因此选 A。

evidence.text: the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously.
evidence.translation: 天才与愚者、富人与穷人都可以同时收听。
evidence.hint: 两组相对身份共同覆盖不同人群，强调人人可用；accessible 在这里指能使用、能接触，并非专指交通便利。

questions.stem: What is the theme of the exhibition at the Bodleian in Oxford?
questions.stemZh: 牛津博德利图书馆这场展览的主题是什么？

options.text: The impact of radio on its early audience.
options.meaning: 广播对早期听众的影响。impact：影响；early audience：早期听众。

options.text: The role of radio in public music education.
options.meaning: 广播在公众音乐教育中的作用。role：作用；public music education：公众音乐教育。

options.text: The innovation process of radio technology.
options.meaning: 广播技术的创新过程。innovation：创新；process：过程。

options.text: The eminent pioneers in radio broadcasting.
options.meaning: 广播事业中杰出的先驱人物。eminent：杰出的、著名的；pioneer：先驱。

questions.explanation: 第二段明确说展览记录了1922至1939年间广播如何改变日常生活，A 对应早期听众所受的影响。

evidence.text: Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939.
evidence.translation: 本周推出的、由比蒂·鲁本斯在牛津博德利图书馆策划的书籍与展览，记录了广播在一九二二至一九三九年间如何改变日常生活。
evidence.hint: 先抓主干 a book and exhibition records how…；how 从句说明展览内容，年份限定了 early audience。

questions.trap: 广播音乐只是后文的一种生活影响，B 把展览的整体主题缩成了单一的音乐教育。

questions.stem: It is indicated in Paragraph 4 that____
questions.stemZh: 第4段表明了什么？

options.text: the research on radio used to be inadequate.
options.meaning: 过去有关广播的研究不充分。used to：过去曾经；inadequate：不足的、不充分的。

options.text: the charm of radio remains in the digital age.
options.meaning: 广播的魅力在数字时代仍然存在。charm：魅力；remain：仍然存在；digital age：数字时代。

options.text: radio listeners could make unexpected gains.
options.meaning: 广播听众可能获得意想不到的收获。unexpected：意料之外的；gain：收获。

options.text: radio shows have changed little over the years.
options.meaning: 多年来，广播节目几乎没有变化。little：几乎没有；over the years：这些年来。

questions.explanation: 第四段提到 serendipity 和随机丰富旅途/劳动的经历，并举作者意外学到听诊器历史为例，C 对应意外收获。

evidence.text: True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task.
evidence.translation: 的确，在数字时代到来前的八十多年里，线性语音广播带来了一种偶然发现的馈赠，能出人意料地为驾车旅途或枯燥劳动增添趣味。
evidence.hint: 逗号后的 random enlivening 解释 serendipity：并非预先安排，而是偶然得到的收获，对应 unexpected gains。

questions.stem: The expression “talking on the brush handle” in Paragraphs 3 and 6 refers to the act of____
questions.stemZh: 第3段和第6段中“talking on the brush handle”这一表达指的是什么行为？

options.meaning: 发出很大的噪声。make a loud noise：发出很响的声音。
随意闲聊。casual：随意的、非正式的；chat：闲聊。
为琐事吵起来。start：引起、开始；trivial：琐碎的；quarrel：争吵。
哼唱一首流行歌曲。hum：哼唱；popular song：流行歌曲。

questions.explanation: 第三段将它与街头交流减少相连，末段怀念邻里习惯；talking on the brush handle 是扶着扫帚闲聊，选 B。

evidence.text: A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and “talking on the brush handle”.
evidence.translation: 一位女士说，广播出现后，街头打架减少了，但人们停下脚步、扶着扫帚闲聊的情况也少了。
evidence.hint: but also 并列的是另一种减少的活动，不是在解释 street fights；该短语要结合末段的 neighbourly habit 理解。

evidence.text: it lost the neighbourly habit of “talking on the brush handle”
evidence.translation: 街上失去了邻里之间扶着扫帚闲聊的习惯。

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author intends to express the opinion that____
questions.stemZh: 作者在最后一段想表达什么观点？

options.text: technology should be aimed at benefiting humans.
options.meaning: 技术应以造福人类为目标。be aimed at：旨在；benefit：使受益、造福。

options.text: actions should be taken to revive the art of listening.
options.meaning: 应采取行动，让倾听的艺术复兴。take actions：采取行动；revive：使复兴。

options.text: adolescents should form healthy social media habits.
options.meaning: 青少年应养成健康的社交媒体使用习惯。adolescent：青少年；form habits：养成习惯。

options.text: people should adopt a sensible attitude to innovations.
options.meaning: 人们应以理性的态度对待创新。adopt：采取；sensible：明智的、理性的；attitude：态度。

sections.title: Reading · Text 4
sections.subtitle: 36–40题 · 10分
sections.directions: Read the following text. Answer the questions after the text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.

paragraphs.en: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to “put everything out,” he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent. Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
paragraphs.zh: 汤姆·斯韦特纳姆回忆说，20世纪70年代他加入美国林务局时，接到的任务是“把所有火都扑灭”。但后来，他进入亚利桑那大学树轮研究实验室攻读研究生，惊讶地发现：在欧洲殖民者来到这片大陆之前的数百年里，这里就反复发生过火灾。他分析的一些树木，其年轮中留有20多处火疤。

paragraphs.en: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier. They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
paragraphs.zh: 火灾发生得如此频繁，意味着这些火不可能猛烈到足以杀死大多数树木。相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁但烈度低的火灾会让许多生态系统更加健康。它们清除了林中的死树和病树，减少了竞争，并遏制疾病传播。由于可燃物无法在地表不断积累，火势往往蔓延缓慢，并在到达先前烧过的地段时逐渐熄灭。

paragraphs.en: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month. In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
paragraphs.zh: 2022年，斯韦特纳姆与其他科学家合作，建立了一个收录北美大陆各地带有火疤树木的数据库。他们的“北美树轮火疤网络”（NAFSN）为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。在这项研究中，研究人员把历史上的火灾发生频率与过去几十年记录的野火进行比较，发现实际火灾次数明显不足。NAFSN各观测点经历的火灾次数，还不到假如没有人为灭火干预时预计会发生次数的四分之一。

paragraphs.en: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. “Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions.”
paragraphs.zh: 国际荒野火灾协会前主席凯莉·马丁说，这种火灾次数的减少证明了现代灭火工作的有效性。“然而，灭火与气候变化共同造成的后果，已经削弱了人类扑灭火灾的能力，尤其是扑灭那些在最危险天气条件下燃起的火灾的能力。”

paragraphs.en: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient. These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 马丁说，要防止整个生态系统毁于大火，人们必须把有益的火带回需要它的地方。在优胜美地国家公园，马丁监督实施了所谓的“计划烧除”，以提高当地景观生态系统的恢复能力。这些火经过周密规划，在天气使火势容易控制的时期有意点燃，帮助清除公园重要设施周围已经积累的部分可燃物。研究表明，这些计划烧除能降低后续野火的烈度，即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下也是如此。

paragraphs.en: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. “It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging,” said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，专家说，尽管科学家和政府官员越来越认同森林中需要更多火灾，气候变化却使这种做法更具挑战性。华盛顿大学火生态学家苏珊·普里查德说：“这是一把双刃剑，因为气候变化使野火越来越猛烈、规模越来越大，我们因而更加需要这项工作；但与此同时，这项工作也变得更加困难。”

notes.translation: 火灾发生得如此频繁，意味着这些火不可能猛烈到足以杀死大多数树木。
notes.hint: 主干是 The fact ... meant ...；that fires happened so often是同位语从句，说明fact的具体内容。couldn’t have been是对过去情况的否定推断；enough to kill ...说明严重程度达到的结果。

notes.translation: NAFSN各观测点经历的火灾次数，还不到假如没有人为灭火干预时预计会发生次数的四分之一。
notes.hint: 主干是 The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of ...。that引导定语从句修饰the number of fires；without fire suppression暗含假设条件，would have been expected表示与实际历史不同的假设结果。比较的是实际次数与无干预时的预计次数。

notes.translation: 研究表明，这些计划烧除能降低后续野火的烈度，即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下也是如此。

options.meaning: 有必要引入计划烧除。necessary：必要的；introduce：引入、采用；prescribed burn：计划烧除。

options.meaning: 加倍投入火灾探测工作会带来回报。rewarding：有回报的、值得做的；double：使加倍；fire detection：火灾探测。

evidence.text: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it.
evidence.translation: 马丁说，要防止整个生态系统毁于大火，人们必须把有益的火带回需要它的地方。

evidence.translation: 我们更加需要这项工作，但与此同时，这项工作也变得更加困难。

sections.title: 新题型 · 段落排序
sections.subtitle: 41–45题 · 10分
sections.directions:
The following paragraphs are given in a wrong order. For questions 41–45, you are required to reorganize these paragraphs into a coherent text by choosing from the list A–H and filling them into the numbered boxes. Paragraphs F, H and C have been correctly placed. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
原卷顺序框：F → 41 → 42 → H → 43 → C → 44 → 45。

paragraphs.en: A. And just read a single poem. In his Oxford lectures, Seamus Heaney argued that a poem draws a picture of reality, a “glimpsed alternative” that sets up a contradiction with your own, in ways little and large. The negotiation, between you and it, is the heart of the matter. What does the poet see that you don't? What does the difference mean? It could be one of the best conversations you ever have. Forget self-help books; reading is self-help in action.
paragraphs.zh: A. 那就读一首诗吧。在牛津讲座中，谢默斯·希尼认为，一首诗会描画现实，为人提供一种“偶然瞥见的另一种可能”，它在大大小小的方面与你的现实形成矛盾。你与诗之间的协商，才是问题的核心。诗人看到了什么而你没有看到？这种差异意味着什么？这可能是你一生中最精彩的对话之一。忘掉自助书吧；阅读就是付诸实践的自我帮助。

paragraphs.en: B. But for the most part, this isn't what the business community does. I have yet to meet a chief executive who reads regularly. Many skip newspapers, and magazines are a stretch. They don't have time, they say. It's inefficient; they can get the information they need from those around them. At a pinch, they might pick up a business book before a long flight, in the hope that, like a cookbook, it will provide a foolproof recipe. Some are drawn to what I think of as “business car crash” books—the stories of Theranos, Purdue, or WeWork. But outside those narrow pools of interest, a vast ocean awaits, bountiful with simmering ideas, mental adventure and imaginative refreshment.
paragraphs.zh: B. 然而，大多数时候，商界并不这样做。我还没有遇到哪位首席执行官有经常阅读的习惯。很多人连报纸也不看，更别说杂志了。他们说自己没有时间。阅读效率太低；他们可以从身边人那里获得所需信息。实在没有办法时，他们或许会在长途飞行前拿起一本商业书，指望它像食谱一样，提供一种万无一失的方法。有些人喜欢我所谓的“商业车祸”书——Theranos、Purdue 或 WeWork 的故事。但在这些狭窄的兴趣池塘之外，有一片浩瀚海洋正等着他们，里面满是酝酿中的思想、心智的冒险和想象力的新生。

paragraphs.en: C. Neuroscientists have been at pains to demonstrate that the pleasure a book provides isn't indulgence; it's good for you. Reading will keep you better informed about the world but it can also improve our tech-shattered ability to concentrate. Standing in the shoes of others fine tunes our social understanding, useful as we struggle to understand friends, neighbours, customers and co-workers. Different parts of our brain engage as we simulate scenes, characters and mental states. Our imagination—remember that?—is rekindled.
paragraphs.zh: C. 神经科学家一直竭力证明，书籍带来的快乐并非放纵；阅读对你有益。阅读使你更了解世界，还可以改善我们被科技打得支离破碎的专注能力。设身处地站在他人的立场，能微调我们的社会理解力，这有助于我们努力理解朋友、邻居、客户和同事。当我们模拟场景、人物和心理状态时，大脑的不同部位会参与其中。我们的想象力——还记得它吗？——重新被点燃了。

paragraphs.en: D. It is undoubtedly true that all work and no play really does make Jack, or Jill, dull. The cure is right at hand. Reading is cheap, easy and, most important, it's fun. Liberate your imagination this year.
paragraphs.zh: D. 毋庸置疑，只工作不玩耍，真的会让杰克或者吉尔变得乏味。良方就在手边。阅读便宜、容易，而且最重要的是，它充满乐趣。今年就释放你的想象力吧。

paragraphs.en: E. We are living through a golden age of science writing, so lucid and accessible that even lay readers can relish the unpredictability of discovery. Daunted by uncertainty? Stand in the shoes of scientists and witness the degree to which breakthroughs emerge from accidents, conflict and sheer mental stamina. “We are never sure of anything,” says the physicist (and writer) Carlo Rovelli.
paragraphs.zh: E. 我们正处于科学写作的黄金时代，作品清晰易懂，甚至外行读者也能享受发现过程的不可预测性。害怕不确定性吗？站在科学家的立场，看看突破有多大程度来自偶然、冲突和纯粹的精神毅力。物理学家兼作家卡洛·罗韦利说：“我们从来无法对任何事情完全确定。”

paragraphs.en: F. You don't need to get out more. If, like most business people, you spend your life dashing from office to plane, train to home, boardroom to washroom, what you really need to do is stay in more, sit down—and read a book.
paragraphs.zh: F. 你不需要更多地出门。如果你像多数商界人士那样，一生都在办公室与飞机、火车与家、会议室与洗手间之间奔波，那么你真正需要的，是多待在家里，坐下来——读一本书。

paragraphs.en: G. Reading has also been found to make us more helpful, to reduce bias, and even to increase longevity—something we will enjoy all the more if we have a good book in our hands. (And yes, all these benefits are more closely associated with physical books than digital ones.)
paragraphs.zh: G. 研究还发现，阅读能使我们更乐于助人、减少偏见，甚至延年益寿——如果手里有一本好书，我们对长寿也会享受得更多。（没错，所有这些好处与纸质书的联系，都比与电子书的联系更紧密。）

paragraphs.en: H. Read fiction. Any fiction. Free yourself from algorithms and choose—anything. You don't need technology for an immersive experience—just surrender to · narratives across time and place. Modern (Sebastian Barry or Olga Tokarczuk), classic (Virginia Woolf or James Baldwin) or genre (Stephen King, Margaret Atwood, Georges Simenon) —it doesn't matter. paragraphs.en: Science education today revolves around the idea of scientific literacy—the base-level knowledge about science that nonscientists require to effectively get on in the world. This concept has served as a central goal for curriculum developers, local school boards, business and community leaders, and policymakers ever since its introduction nearly 80 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，科学教育围绕“科学素养”这一理念展开，即非科学工作者为了有效应对现实生活而需要具备的基本科学知识。这个概念自近八十年前提出以来，就一直是课程开发者、地方学校董事会、商界与社区领袖以及政策制定者的核心目标。

paragraphs.en: (46) Tracing the history of the term, we can see how the definition of scientific literacy has shifted over time, muddying the waters when it comes to determining the goals of science education. And that's a shame, because there is much to recommend in the idea of scientific literacy as it was originally articulated in 1945, a time when science appeared to be the key to progress and scientists seemingly held the fate of the world in their hands. (47) A return to that version of scientific literacy, which focused more on teaching what science is and how it works and less on memorizing scientific facts, seems like something society today desperately needs.
paragraphs.zh: （46）追溯这个术语的历史，我们就能看到科学素养的定义如何随时间发生变化，而在确定科学教育的目标时，这种变化又使问题变得模糊不清。这令人遗憾，因为一九四五年最初提出科学素养理念时，其中有许多可取之处；那时，科学似乎是进步的关键，而科学家仿佛掌握着世界的命运。（47）回归那种科学素养理念，也就是更重视教授科学是什么、如何运作，而较少强调记忆科学事实的理念，似乎是当今社会迫切需要的。

paragraphs.en: In the United States, the desire to provide the public with a general, nontechnical education in science originated as far back as the late 1800s. (48) Educators advanced the idea of having students complete detailed laboratory exercises in high schools in the belief that such work was beneficial primarily as a way to enhance logical reasoning and observational skills. The development in 1915 of the popular new subject “general science” was another effort to train students to apply the principles of science to everyday, nonscience problems.
paragraphs.zh: 在美国，向公众提供一般性、非专业的科学教育的愿望，最早可以追溯到十九世纪末。（48）教育工作者提出，让高中生完成详尽的实验室练习，因为他们认为这类工作主要有利于增强逻辑推理与观察能力。一九一五年广受欢迎的新学科“普通科学”的发展，则是又一次尝试，旨在训练学生将科学原理应用于日常的非科学问题。

paragraphs.en: Although these efforts were aimed at the nonscience-bound student, they never really made their way into mainstream thought and public discourse as a means to rally widespread support for the importance of science teaching in schools. (49) It wasn't until the phrase “scientific literacy” came along in the 1940s that science had the formidable slogan it needed to command public attention and make improving science education an important national goal.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管这些努力面向的是未来不从事科学工作的学生，但它们始终没有真正进入主流思想和公共讨论，成为争取公众广泛支持学校科学教育重要性的一种方式。（49）直到二十世纪四十年代“科学素养”这一说法出现，科学才拥有了吸引公众关注所需要的响亮口号，并使改进科学教育成为重要的国家目标。

paragraphs.en: (50) The intense focus on scientific literacy in the United States originally grew out of the critical role of science and technology during World War I, as well as the perceived deficiencies of American soldiers. As the war unfolded, science rapidly assumed a central role. Battles increasingly depended on new military technologies such as radar and the proximity fuze. Science-based analytical approaches proved remarkably successful in the hunt for German submarines in the Atlantic Ocean. And there was the (then-secret) work building the world's first atomic bomb. As a result, scientists— physicists in particular—found themselves in high demand.
paragraphs.zh: （50）美国最初高度重视科学素养，源于科学技术在第一次世界大战期间发挥的关键作用，以及人们所认为的美国士兵存在的不足。随着战争展开，科学迅速处于核心地位。战斗越来越依赖雷达和近炸引信等新军事技术。在大西洋追踪德国潜艇时，基于科学的分析方法被证明极为成功。此外，还有当时处于保密状态的研制世界第一颗原子弹的工作。因此，科学家——尤其是物理学家——变得十分抢手。【资料提示：用户提供的原卷第50题印为 World War I，但后文雷达、原子弹等例子涉及二战；此处忠实保留原卷表述。】

questions.answer: 直到二十世纪四十年代“科学素养”这一说法出现，科学才拥有了吸引公众注意所需要的响亮口号，并使改善科学教育成为一项重要的国家目标。
questions.explanation: It wasn’t until…that…是“直到……才……”强调句。it needed 修饰 slogan，to command…and make…说明 slogan 的作用。make 后为“宾语＋宾补”。

questions.stem: The intense focus on scientific literacy in the United States originally grew out of the critical role of science and technology during World War I, as well as the perceived deficiencies of American soldiers.

questions.answer: 美国最初对科学素养的高度重视，源于科学技术在第一次世界大战中发挥的关键作用，以及人们所认为的美国士兵存在的不足。

questions.answer:
Dear Paul,

I am glad that you enjoyed the handwritten family letters I posted. They were written by Chinese people working or studying far from home. Besides sharing news, the writers expressed their love for their families and hopes for the future. These ordinary words make the letters precious records of family life.

Some of the letters are now on public display at our local museum. The exhibition is open from Tuesday to Sunday, and admission is free. If you are available, we could visit it together this weekend.

Best regards,
Li Ming

questions.stemZh: 根据养老机器人调查图表写160—200词短文，包含描述、解释与评论。
questions.answer:
The two charts present consumers’ acceptance of elderly-care robots and their primary concerns. While 39.3% fully accept such robots and 32.8% accept them partially, 27.9% reject them. Safety is the leading concern, at 46.3%, followed by price at 24.9% and convenience at 10.7%. These figures suggest an attitude of interest mixed with caution.

Several factors may explain this pattern. An aging population and busy working lives create a growing demand for assistance with daily care. Robots could remind older people to take medicine, help with routine tasks and alert family members in emergencies. However, caring for vulnerable people requires dependable technology. Consumers naturally worry about mechanical failures, privacy and the ability of machines to respond appropriately. The cost can also prevent ordinary families from adopting these products.

In my view, elderly-care robots can be useful partners in care. Manufacturers should put safety first, offer clear evidence from testing and work to make reliable products affordable. Meanwhile, families should remember that technology can support practical care, while personal attention and emotional companionship remain essential.
questions.explanation: 本范文由模型编写，供学习参考，不是唯一标准答案。首段准确描述：完全接受39.3%、部分接受32.8%、不接受27.9%；首要关注安全46.3%、价格24.9%、便利10.7%。柱状图只列出三个关注点，合计不为100%，不能据此补写未知项目。第二段解释需求与顾虑，第三段评论安全、价格及人文关怀。
